broken_vs_unusable: broken means the declaration is malformed and gates the exit code. unusable means every link holds and the matcher still recovers nothing — a real set the pipeline cannot reach. Those definitions say DO NOT USE; they are kept declared so the failure stays visible and so they start working when the abbreviation resolver lands.
licence: identifiers and counts only; no UMLS string appears here
membership_not_linking: a probe returning a different CUI inside the set is a success. found_exact is the stricter linking rate, reported separately.
probe: each concept's own preferred English string is fed to the real matcher; found_in_set means the answer was a member, which is what phenotype evidence tests. A shortest-string probe runs beside it, and the signed delta between them is negative for five of eight: UMLS preferred terms carry qualifiers the matcher cannot absorb, so the bare short atom is often the easier surface, not the harder.
question: does every declared phenotype have concepts linked to it, all the way to text?
reachability_is_not_recall: self-name reachability is necessary and not sufficient, and it does NOT estimate measured_set_recall. Every concept counts once here while real evidence is dominated by a few common ones, so the two diverge in both directions: chronic_kidney_disease 0.349 vs 0.889 (a poorly-matching tail no note writes), heart_failure 0.863 vs 0.449 (concepts reachable by their own names, surfaces clinicians type that are not). Read this for broken links; read measured_set_recall for how much evidence a run will find.
why: a non-empty concept set is not the question. A set the matcher cannot emit is functionally empty and fails silently: the run reports evidence_touch 0, which reads exactly like a note that never mentioned the phenotype.
